description: Run the PRODUCTION build in a browser: build the project, serve it, and launch. There is no hot module replacement, so your edits are not picked up; use extension_dev while writing code, and this to check what actually ships. By default there is no control channel either, so extension_eval, extension_storage, extension_reload, extension_open and extension_dom_snapshot cannot attach. Pass allowControl:true (or allowEval:true, which implies it) to drive the production run with them: the browser then loads a copy of the build with the control producer added, dist/<browser> keeps the shipped bytes, and extension_reload reloads the installed extension under open tabs the way a store update does, which is how to test content scripts an update orphans. Both flags need Extension.js 4.1.34, not yet released; a project on 4.1.33 is refused as engine-unsupported, naming the flag, and extension_dev drives the run instead. Pass build:false to launch an existing dist/<browser> without rebuilding, or outputPath to launch any prebuilt unpacked extension directory, one another toolchain produced included, which implies build:false. The answer says what it confirmed (the engine process, and the browser pid the launcher recorded once the contract lands) and what a production session cannot confirm (that the browser loaded the extension: it opens no debug port and has no console stream), and names extension_dev for a proven load.

allowControl.description: Open the agent-bridge control channel on the production run, so extension_storage, extension_reload, extension_open and extension_dom_snapshot reach it. The browser loads a copy of the build with the control producer prepended to the background; dist/<browser> is not changed. Needs an engine whose start verb takes --allow-control (the published 4.1.33 does not).

allowEval.description: Also enable extension_eval on the production run (writes a 0600 session token). Implies allowControl. The build's own content_security_policy still governs eval in its extension pages and background.

build.description: Build before serving. false serves the existing dist/<browser> as-is and fails when there is none.

chromiumBinary.description: Custom Chromium-based binary to launch; `browser` still names the target family the engine builds for (chromium-based when none is given).

extensions.description: Extra extension paths or store URLs to load alongside the project

geckoBinary.description: Custom Gecko/Firefox binary to launch; `browser` still names the target family the engine builds for (gecko-based when none is given).

headless.description: false opens a browser window the person can see, overriding EXTENSION_HEADLESS and any --headless in EXTENSION_BROWSER_FLAGS for this session only; pass it when the person wants to watch or try the extension. true forces headless. Omit to inherit the environment (headless when EXTENSION_HEADLESS=1 or EXTENSION_BROWSER_FLAGS carries --headless).

host.description: Bind host, default 127.0.0.1. Use 0.0.0.0 in Docker or devcontainers.

noBrowser.description: Build (or, with build:false, check the dist) without launching a browser. A production start serves nothing, so with no browser the engine process ends once the build does; read the result with extension_build rather than a session.

outputPath.description: An existing unpacked extension directory to launch as it is (a manifest.json at its root), for an artifact built by another toolchain or an exact release candidate. Implies build:false; projectPath still names the project the session belongs to. Relative paths resolve against projectPath.

port.description: Passed to the engine as --port (0 for auto-assign). A production start serves nothing over it today; it matters only to a toolchain that reads it.

profile.description: Profile path, or "false" to reuse the real user profile. Omit for a throwaway one.

publicHost.description: Host the browser dials for HMR and reload when it differs from the bind host

replace.description: Stop the live session this projectPath runs for the same browser first (an extension_dev or extension_start session), reported as replacedSession. Without it the call is refused: one session per browser owns dist/<browser> and its ready.json and eval token, and a production start would rebuild them under the running session. A session for another browser keeps running either way.

startingUrl.description: URL the browser opens on launch

name: extension_start
